name: Union Pacific Jack Koraleski Technology, Research & Development Center

profile.address: Union Pacific Jack Koraleski Technology, Research & Development Center, 8949, Sorensen Parkway, Irvington, Omaha, Union Precinct, Douglas County, Nebraska, 68122
profile.reading:
This facility at 8949 Sorensen Parkway in the Irvington area of north Omaha, Nebraska, carries the name of Jack Koraleski, a longtime Union Pacific executive who rose through the company's marketing and sales organization to serve as vice chairman before being named chief executive officer, a position he held until his retirement in 2015. Koraleski was later inducted into the University of Nebraska Omaha business hall of fame in recognition of his career at the railroad. Naming a major operational or technology building after a former senior executive is a common practice among large, long established railroads, and Union Pacific has followed that pattern here.

Union Pacific Railroad, together with its parent Union Pacific Corporation, is one of North America's largest Class I freight railroads, moving agricultural, industrial, energy, and intermodal freight across a network spanning the western two thirds of the United States. The company's corporate headquarters sits downtown at Union Pacific Center, a 317 foot office tower at 1400 Douglas Street that opened in June 2004. This Sorensen Parkway address, several miles north of downtown near Omaha's Eppley Airfield, is a separate location from that headquarters tower, consistent with a dedicated technology or research building rather than general office space.

Large freight railroads depend on extensive, continuously available information technology to run functions such as train dispatching and network scheduling, shipment tracking, safety systems including federally mandated positive train control, and customer facing logistics platforms, all of which require reliable data center capacity somewhere in the company's real estate footprint. It is reasonable to expect a building carrying a technology and research and development designation, bearing a former CEO's name, and located apart from the main headquarters to serve some part of that function for Union Pacific's own operations. However, Union Pacific has not published a facility description, opening date, capacity figure, or specific account of what research or technology work takes place inside this particular building, so its exact role within the company's broader technology infrastructure is not something that can be confirmed from public materials, only inferred from the company's operational needs and the building's name and location.
